subject: Commitment ladder & activation windows for CrossBeam deployment
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>

Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Commitment ladder & activation windows for CrossBeam deployment

Hi Sarah —

Great speaking yesterday. Per our chat, attached is a compact set of commitment ladder options so your infrastructure and procurement teams can see predictable pricing + activation plans without overcommitting. High level (see attached PDF for full tables):

Option A — Lean baseline (fast onramp)
- Minimum committed GPUs: 8 A100-equivalent
- Activation window: 30 days after signature
- Burst lanes: +4 GPUs for 2× sustained 2-hour windows/day
- Ideal for product-phase testing and limited inference workloads

Option B — Staged growth (rolling ladder)
- Start: 12 GPUs, increase to 24 GPUs after month 3, 48 GPUs by month 9
- Activation windows: 14–60 days per tranche
- Pricing: blended unit rates with step-downs at each tranche

Option C — Performance anchored (steady-state)
- Minimum committed GPUs: 32
- Reserved throughput SLOs (99th pct latency targets)
- Capacity buffer and guaranteed burst of +16 GPUs

Questions for you so we can finalize numbers:
1) Target steady-state QPS for peak hour? (rough tokens/sec or calls/min)
2) Any hard procurement start/end dates or PO cadence?
3) Which region(s) must be guaranteed for production?

Attached: CrossBeam_Commitment_Ladder_v3.pdf (detailed ramp tables) and crossbeam_cost-model_v2.xlsx (cost model by tranche).

If you like, we can sketch a DocuSign-ready agreement with Option B as default and a 60-day activation buffer for the first tranche.

Thanks,
Sofia

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-09-06T11:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Commitment ladder & activation windows for CrossBeam deployment

Looping in recommended sizing based on CrossBeam's QPS guidance. My quick notes (assumes rw-v2-70B-q4 weights for generation; smaller embed/rerank models not included):

- 3k calls/min (steady peak) ≈ sustained 10k tokens/min; target 99th latency 200–300ms for chat endpoints.
- GPU mapping (A100-equivalent):
  • 8 GPUs — supports low single-digit k calls/min with tight batching + prefix caches (Option A).
  • 12–16 GPUs — safe initial tranche to hit 3k calls/min with headroom (recommended start).
  • 32 GPUs — steady-state for 9k calls/min with burst headroom and SLOs.

Operational notes:
- Recommend a 2-week warm-up period per tranche for KV cache population and perf tuning.
- Keep one lane in the pool for canary traffic (2 GPUs) to validate rollouts.
- If they require eu-west as active DR, plan symmetric minimums there (adds ~40% to committed footprint or use cross-region failover).

I attached the updated cost sheet (crossbeam_cost-model_v2.xlsx) with GPU-hours, burst assumptions, and an example 9-month ramp. If procurement needs quarter-aligned tranches we can shift activation windows to Oct 1 / Jan 1 etc.

Ben
Ben Carter
Lead Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah —

Thanks — I incorporated Ben's sizing notes and aligned the first tranche to Oct 1 per procurement preference. Summary of the updated proposal:

- Proposed default: Option B (staged growth) with quarter-aligned tranches
  • Tranche 1 (Oct 1): 16 GPUs (us-west), 2 GPUs reserved for canary
  • Tranche 2 (Jan 1): +16 GPUs (total 32)
  • Tranche 3 (Apr 1): +16 GPUs (total 48) — optional based on usage triggers
- Geo: Primary active in us-west; eu-west set as async DR unless you opt for symmetric active replication (adds ~40% cost).
- Onboarding: 14-day activation window per tranche + 14-day warm-up before full SLA enforcement.
- Flex: 30% burst lanes available for 60 minutes/day during launch weeks at pre-agreed unit rates.

Next steps:
1) Procurement confirms quarter starts and signs the DocuSign envelope (link below).
2) We schedule a 30-min ops runbook call to map canary lanes, DR behavior, and alert thresholds.
3) Redwood to deliver final DocuSign and a short playbook for the 14-day warm-up.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/envelopes/ABC-123-crossbeam
Ops runbook call — proposed times: Tue 2026-09-14 10am PDT or Wed 2026-09-15 1pm PDT. Which works for you?

Thanks,
